concerns.text: FR-005 proposes partial correlation between motif z-scores and rsFC metrics controlling for 'global node degree'. This creates a circular/tautological validation risk: motif z-scores are defined relative to a degree-preserving null model (FR-004). If the 'global node degree' control variable is the structural degree, it is already factored into the z-score definition, making the partial correlation testing a residual of a residual that may not be statistically independent. If the control is functional degree, it is a component of the rsFC outcome (global efficiency), creating a tautology. The spec must explicitly define the source of the control variable and justify its independence from the predictor's definition.

FR-005 requires running 13 separate partial correlations without addressing multicollinearity between motif z-scores. In a fixed-size graph, motif counts are structurally coupled (e.,g., an increase in feedforward loops implies a decrease in others). Running univariate tests on highly correlated predictors inflates Type I error rates beyond what Bonferroni correction (designed for independent outcomes) can handle. The methodology is unsound without a multivariate approach (e.,g., LASSO, PCA, or joint regression) or explicit VIF filtering.

The validation target 'global efficiency' (derived from rsFC) is a deterministic function of the rsFC matrix edge weights. Correlating structural motif z-scores (predictor) with a global summary of the functional network (outcome) tests a relationship between two aggregate scalars. This fails to address the research question 'Do specific network motif configurations... constrain individual variation in rsFC patterns?' which implies edge-level or regional correspondence. Using a global scalar outcome creates a 'global-to-global' correlation that may mask local structural constraints and is methodologically insufficient for the claimed hypothesis.

The spec assumes a 'binary structural adjacency matrix' but does not explicitly commit to directed vs. undirected graph topology. HCP diffusion data is inherently directed (streamline counts). The Maslov-Sneppen rewiring null model and the set of 3-node motifs differ fundamentally between directed (13 motifs) and undirected (4 motifs) regimes. Using an undirected null model on directed data (or vice versa) invalidates the z-score calculation. The spec must explicitly define the graph directionality assumption to ensure the null model and motif enumeration are mathematically consistent.

The power analysis (FR-010) assumes N=50 and Bonferroni correction across ~13 motifs. With alpha ~0.0038, the minimum detectable effect size (r) for 80% power is >0.45. The spec fails to acknowledge that this design has a high probability of Type II error for moderate effect sizes (common in neuroimaging). A null result would be inconclusive, yet the spec treats 'no effect' as a valid finding without addressing this statistical limitation.

The null model (Maslov-Sneppen) preserves degree but destroys higher-order correlations (e.,g., rich-club organization). If the structural connectome has such constraints, the z-scores may be inflated/deflated relative to a more appropriate null. The spec lacks justification for why degree-preserving is sufficient to isolate 'motif-specific' effects from other structural constraints, risking invalid z-score interpretation.
